title: Linux Disks and LVM: What Engineers Need

scenes.line1: Ever had a disk fill up?
scenes.say: Ever had a disk fill up on Linux? How do you fix it when it happens?
Disks break down into partitions. LVM, or Logical Volume Manager, sits on top. Then you add a filesystem like XFS or EXT4, and mount it.

scenes.title: Find what's full
scenes.say: To troubleshoot, use df dash h to see which filesystem is full. du shows what's using space. lsof plus L1 finds deleted files still open.
To extend a disk with LVM, grow the partition, resize the physical volume, then lvextend with dash r to expand the filesystem in one step.

scenes.question: How do you grow an LVM filesystem?
scenes.right: Use lvextend with dash r to grow both the volume and the filesystem at once.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Don't just run lvextend and then resize2fs. Use lvextend with dash r to grow both the volume and the filesystem at once.
